purpose: design how data is stored, owned, moved and protected, so it stays correct, available and compliant
entry_criteria: Requirements and data needs are known
procedure: Identify the main data entities, who owns each, and where the system of record is.
Choose storage types per need (transactional, analytical, search, cache) and justify each.
Design how data moves between systems, how often, and how consistency is kept.
Define retention, archiving, deletion and backup rules for each class of data.
Design access control and protection by classification, including masking in non-production.
Document lineage for key data and the quality checks that guard it.
acceptance_criteria: Each entity has one system of record and an owner
Retention and deletion rules exist per class
Non-production data is masked or synthetic
validation_method: Data architect and data owner approval.

validation.check: check every entity in the model lists a system of record and an owner
check each personal-data field has a retention rule

failure_modes.response: Choose one and sync from it

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Customer data is owned by the account service; the warehouse receives a nightly copy with email masked, and personal fields are deleted 24 months after account closure.
